title: billing-and-entitlements-release-orchestration-and-sales-launch-plan
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Coordinate the launch of the tiered pricing and SKU/entitlements consolidation across billing, console, docs, and sales. This ticket captures the runbook for release notes, cross-team dependencies, customer migration steps, canary gating, and sales enablement materials. Goal: ship a low-friction migration path for existing customers, clear release notes and in-product messaging, and sales collateral to prevent friction during renewals.

Scope: SKU mapping, default rate limits per tier, prorated billing behavior, entitlement assignment during migration, API contract changes (new 'billing_sku' field and limits headers), console UI copy and banners, release notes, support playbooks, partner comms. Not in scope: price negotiations for individual enterprise contracts (handled by Sales - separate playbook).

Spec prorated billing algorithm and sign-off (Finance + Billing)
Implement entitlement migration script and dry-run on staging (ENG)
Create in-console migration banner + help center link (Product + Design)
Draft release notes: user-facing changes + migration steps + API migration guide (PM + Docs)
Prepare customer email templates segmented by tier and usage (Growth + CS)
Create sales enablement pack: one-pager, objection FAQ, pricing calculator, slide deck (PM + Sales Enablement)
Instrument telemetry: billing delta dashboard, migration success rate, support ticket surge alerts (Observability)
Define rollback criteria and emergency billing patch playbook (PM + ENG + Billing)
Schedule customer webinars and AM-only office hours for migrations (CS + Solutions)
Coordinate rate-limit enforcement roll windows and feature flags (ENG)
QA and sign-off for release notes and API docs (Docs + Legal)
Prepare PRs and release tags for billing and console components (ENG)
Create internal comms timeline for all teams and partner teams (PM)
Train support and renewals on migration steps and compensation policy (CS + Sales)
Publish post-launch monitoring dashboard and run daily triage for week 0 (Observability + PM)

release_notes_draft: What changed: Consolidated SKUs into three tiered packages with clearer limits and entitlements
Why: Reduce confusion, improve predictability of unit economics, and simplify usage quotas
Who is affected: All customers; most will be auto-migrated. Enterprise customers on custom contracts are excluded unless they opt in
Migration: We will auto-map existing SKUs to the closest tier and apply prorated billing for the transition month. See 'How to check your mapped tier' below

API impact: New response header 'X-Redwood-Quota-Limit' and optional 'billing_sku' field in usage endpoints. Backwards compatible; older clients continue to work but should consume new header for quota UI
Support: Dedicated migration support and office hours for first two weeks post-launch
Rollout plan and rollback criteria summarized at the end of the notes
sales_enablement_assets: Sales slide deck and speaker notes (link: https://drive.redwood.ai/sales-deck)
Cheat-sheet for renewals: migration concessions and credits policy
Recorded enablement session and Q&A transcript
rollout_plan: Canary: 5% of customers by usage cohort (low token volume) for 72h
Evaluate canary metrics: billing delta < 2%, migration success rate > 99%, support tickets minimal
Ramp to 25% for 72h if metrics OK
Full ramp next maintenance window with rate-limit enforcement and last-mile billing switch
Feature flags to gate per-tenant mapping for immediate rollback
Enterprise customers: manual outreach and opt-in migration with dedicated CS owner
telemetry_and_alerts: Billing delta dashboard: daily billing delta by cohort (expected tolerance +/-2%)
Support ticket surge alert if daily ticket volume related to pricing/migration > 10x baseline
High-severity customer call trigger for any enterprise customer with billing impact > $5000
Realtime console errors and API 5xx rate monitoring during canary and ramp
migration_strategy: Auto-mapping: algorithmic mapping using historical monthly spend and peak usage
Dry-run mode: produce mapping report without changing entitlements (staging & small production cohort)
Opt-out: customers may opt out within 7 days of email notification; opt-out preserves prior entitlements for 1 billing cycle
Proration: implement prorated billing adjustment for the transition month; finance sign-off required
Manual review: flagged edge cases (>5% billing delta) to be routed to Ops for reconciliation
rollback_criteria: Billing delta > 5% across >10% of canary cohort
Support ticket surge > 10x baseline sustained for 24h
Critical API regressions or console outages during ramp
acceptance_criteria: SKU mapping table approved and published
Billing system implements prorated charge logic with test coverage and finance sign-off
Documentation and release notes published and reviewed by Legal
Sales enablement materials completed and distributed
Telemetry dashboards live with alerting and runbook entries
Canary executed and metrics within thresholds before full rollout
